MARVELLE J. BALLENTINE,
Plaintiff,
Case No. 1:26-cv-02331
V.
KATIE HALL, individually;
NATIONAL CENTER FOR MISSING & EXPLOITED
CHILDREN;
META PLATFORMS, INC.;
and JOHN/JANE DOES 1-6,
Defendants.
MEMORANDUM IN SUPPORT OF PLAINTIFF'S RULE 201 REQUEST FOR
JUDICIAL NOTICE
Plaintiff asks the Court to notice one court record for what it is and what it says. The record
is ECF No. 152 in Ballentine v. Meta Platforms, Inc., No. 3:26-cv-05939-RFL (N.D. Cal.), filed
August 13, 2026 and attached as Exhibit A. Plaintiff does not ask the Court to accept any statement
in it as true.
RULE 201 REQUIRES NOTICE OF A COURT RECORD WHOSE EXISTENCE
AND TEXT ARE NOT SUBJECT TO REASONABLE DISPUTE
Federal Rule of Evidence 201(b)(2) permits the Court to notice a fact that "can be
accurately and readily determined from sources whose accuracy cannot reasonably be questioned."
Rule 201(c)(2) provides that the Court "must take judicial notice if a party requests it and the court
is supplied with the necessary information." Rule 201(d) provides that notice may be taken "at any
stage of the proceeding." Plaintiff has requested notice. Exhibit A supplies the information.
1

The Fourth Circuit has stated that "[t]he most frequent use of judicial notice of
ascertainable facts is in noticing the content of court records." Colonial Penn Ins. Co. v. Coil, 887
F.2d 1236, 1239 (4th Cir. 1989) (quoting 21 C. Wright & K. Graham, Federal Practice and
Procedure: Evidence § 5106, at 505 (1977)). The same opinion recognized that "federal courts, in
appropriate circumstances, may take notice of proceedings in other courts, both within and without
the federal judicial system, if those proceedings have a direct relation to matters at issue." Id.
(quoting St. Louis Baptist Temple, Inc. v. FDIC, 605 F.2d 1169, 1172 (10th Cir. 1979)). Colonial
Penn applied those principles on appeal, to state-court guilty pleas entered after the district court's
judgment. Id. at 1239-40. A filing on a federal docket, bearing that court's electronic filing header
on every page, is a court record of the same kind.
Exhibit A is that record. Each of its 25 pages carries the header "Case 3:26-cv-05939-RFL
Document 152 Filed 08/13/26." Its first page states its title. Its signature pages identify its
signatories and their clients. Its footnote 3 appears at ECF pages 11-12. The existence, date,
signatories, and text of ECF No. 152 can be determined from the face of the document. Those facts
are not subject to reasonable dispute.
II.
THE REQUEST IS CONFINED TO EXISTENCE, DATE, AUTHORSHIP, AND
TEXT
The Fourth Circuit has stated that whether a fact may be considered under Rule 201 at the
pleading stage "depends on the manner in which a court uses this information." Zak v. Chelsea
Therapeutics Int'l, Ltd., 780 F.3d 597, 607 (4th Cir. 2015). This Request fixes that manner in
advance. Plaintiff asks the Court to notice that ECF No. 152 was filed on August 13, 2026, that it
bears the title stated in Exhibit A, that it was signed by the counsel identified at Exhibit A pages
3,24, and 25, that footnote 3 reads as quoted in the Request, and that footnote 3 names this action
by case number. Request 9| 4(a)-(e).
2

Plaintiff does not ask the Court to notice that any statement in footnote 3 is true. Plaintiff
does not ask the Court to notice why the footnote was written or what any signatory intended.
Request 1 5. Notice of what a filing says is different from acceptance of what it asserts. The
Request asks for the first and disclaims the second.
III. THE NOTICED FACTS BEAR ON PENDING MATTERS
ECF No. 152 is pleaded in the proposed Second Amended and Supplemental Complaint.
ECF No. 59-1 19 164-169. Paragraph 165 quotes the portion of footnote 3 that describes this
action. ECF No. 59-1 9 165. The supporting memorandum identifies the filing by court, case
number, docket entry, and footnote. ECF No. 60 at 9. Leave to file that pleading was denied. ECF
No. 84 at 2. Plaintiff's objections and motions concerning that denial remain pending. ECF Nos.
89, 90, 93. Plaintiff's motion for leave to amend, filed separately, attaches a Proposed Second
Amended Complaint that also pleads ECF No. 152. Proposed Second Am. Compl. 1 180-185.
The Court's ability to compare the pleaded quotation with the source record serves the
determination of those motions.
Meta and NCMEC have invoked the same mechanism in this action. Meta's memorandum
states that, on a Rule 12(b)(6) motion, a court may consider "matters of which the court may take
judicial notice." ECF No. 22 at 8 (citations and internal quotation marks omitted). NCMEC's
memorandum states that this Court "may take judicial notice" of a proposition about subpoena
practice. ECF No. 11 at 6. Plaintiff asks for less. Plaintiff asks the Court to notice a court record
for its existence, date, signatories, and text.
3

IV.
CONCLUSION
Rule 201(c)(2) is mandatory where a party requests notice and supplies the necessary
information. Plaintiff has done both. The Court should take judicial notice of the five facts stated
in Paragraph 4 of the Request. In the alternative, the Court should take judicial notice of the facts
stated in Paragraph 4(a), (b), (C), and (e).
Date: November 1, 2026
Respectfully submitted,
Marvelle J. Ballentine
Plaintiff, pro se
